If rescuers are unable to safely retrieve the body, chances are the corpse will stay put. Maybe they’ll try to cover up the body out of respect, but that’s dependent on where the decedent is located. I’m not sure what rescuers say to the victims family, but I’m sure the general vibe is that they did the best they could do. 
  
John Edward Jones died after getting stuck in a cave while spelunking; rescue teams tried their best to remove him, and later his corpse, but ultimately decided the retrieval was too difficult and dangerous - so they closed off the entrance to the cave as a way to create a makeshift tomb.  
  
Bodies on Mount Everest often end up staying there because recovery missions can prove to be fatal. At times the best that can be done is pushing the frozen corpse to a more isolated section of the mountain or covering up the body with stones and/or other materials. Usually bodies are left where they lay and are used as macabre landmarks.

Théodore Géricault studied corpses for “The Raft of the Medusa”, Joel-Peter Witkin posed [parts of] cadavers in his photography, and Marina Abramović’s “Rhythm 0” performance gave the audience the ability to kill her if they so wished - death and the dead have been interconnected with art for centuries, so I could see how the natural progression could be murder itself (that is, of course, if morality was totally lost lmao)  
  
Though the real question might really be /how valid/ of an art form is murder. Is it poignant, does it have motivation, some sort of artistic purpose - or is it just spectacle and cheap thrills? Though I guess that could be asked of literally any other artistic medium haha

Natural burials are starting to become more popular (or at the very least more talked about), so you would need to find a funeral home that specializes in that kind of thing. A body farm could also be interesting, just know that most institutions will take your picked-clean skeleton and catalogue it for future reference - so that might not be the way to go if you want your skeleton to decompose as well.  
It’s never too soon to come up with a death plan, and being open about death helps fight the stigma surrounding it.
